newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORDIC SKIING-BLOOD TESTS TO BE PERFORMED AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-BLOOD TESTS TO BE PERFORMED AT WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS.

text.p: Organisers of the Nordic skiing world championships, worried about continuing allegations of blood doping, said blood tests would be carried out during the 10-day festival starting on Friday.
The tests, which have already been introduced in World Cup races, will be performed, for the first time in world championships, on 20 competitors, selected randomly, before each race.

After the races, the first four and two other athletes selected randomly will aslo be tested. The samples will be analysed in Trondheim and in another laboratory accredited by the International Olympic committee in Oslo.
The blood tests will be carried out in addition to the usual urine tests.
"There will be more dope tests than during the 1994 Olympics in Lillehammer and they will be more accurate," said Norwegian Inggard Lereim, the world championships' chief doctor.
Blood testing is aimed at detecting high haemoglobin levels in red blood cells, which boost endurance by enabling the blood to transport more oxygen to working muscles.
The haemoglobin level can increased by taking the blood from an athlete's body and pumping it back just before competition.
Injecting erythropoietin (EPO) has a similar effect as the banned substance stimulates the production of red blood cells.
Studies have shown that extended EPO use can thicken the blood and cause heart-attacks.
"The (blood) tests are aimed not only at making sure that nobody cheats, but also at preventing human tragedies," Lerreim said.

Like cycling, to which the use of EPO has often been linked, Nordic skiing is an extremely demanding sport and blood doping could be used in it to help athletes go beyond what they would achieve without it.
Nordic skiing's top competitors had pressed for blood tests and for defined limits for haemoglobin levels after some abnormally high levels were detected in routine pre-race tests.
The tests were carried out for the first time during competition at a World Cup meeting last month in Hakuba, Japan, where the Nordic skiing events of next year's Nagano Olympics will take place.
